People, characters and animals, and the ties between them.

Every figure here is live: drag a node, hover for a name, and *Open with controls* gives you the same view in a full window with the colouring and layout options exposed. The data, and the script that rebuilds each one from its source, are in the [`networks`](https://github.com/maxjerdee/networks) repository.

## Karate Club {#karate}

```{=html}
<div class="ew-embed" data-network="karate.gml"
     data-params="layout=force&colorAttr=faction&sizeAttr=degree&edgeOpacity=0.3&edgeScale=0.8"
     data-caption="Karate Club — 34 nodes, 78 edges, undirected"></div>
```

| | |
|---|---|
| **A node** | Karate club member, colored by which faction they joined after the club split |
| **An edge** | Observed social tie outside normal club activities |

Zachary, W. W. (1977). An information flow model for conflict and fission in small groups. Journal of Anthropological Research, 33(4), 452-473.

*Wayne W. Zachary · [source](https://networks.skewed.de/net/karate) · [data and build script](https://github.com/maxjerdee/networks/tree/main/networks/karate)*

**Licence.** No licence stated by the source. Published as part of the cited paper, before data licensing was normal, and redistributed widely in the network-science literature since; there is no licence to point to. Cite the paper.

## Friends {#friends}

```{=html}
<div class="ew-embed" data-network="friends.gml"
     data-params="layout=community-attract&colorAttr=class&sizeAttr=degree&edgeOpacity=0.3&edgeScale=0.6"
     data-caption="Friends — 133 nodes, 665 edges, directed"></div>
```

| | |
|---|---|
| **A node** | Student, colored by class (nine classes across four subjects) |
| **An edge** | A → B: A named B as a friend in the survey. One-way: a nomination need not be returned |

Reported friendship network of 329 students in nine classes of a lycee in Marseille, France, December 2013. A directed edge i->j means student i named j as a friend in the survey. Collected by the SocioPatterns collaboration alongside wearable-sensor proximity, contact-diary and Facebook networks for the same school; this is the friendship survey. Mastrandrea, R., Fournet, J., & Barrat, A. (2015). Contact Patterns in a High School: A Comparison between Data Collected Using Wearable Sensors, Contact Diaries and Friendship Surveys. PLOS ONE 10(9), e0136497. Node attribute `class` is a readable name for each of the nine classes, with the original French preparatory-class code kept as `class_code` (a trailing * marks the selective stream of that subject); `field` collapses the nine into the four subjects they study.

*SocioPatterns (R. Mastrandrea, J. Fournet, A. Barrat) · compiled by Max Jerdee · [source](https://www.sociopatterns.org/datasets/high-school-contact-and-friendship-networks/) · [data and build script](https://github.com/maxjerdee/networks/tree/main/networks/friends)*

**Licence.** Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 3.0 (CC BY-NC-SA 3.0), as stated by SocioPatterns. Redistribution permitted with attribution; non-commercial; a redistributed derivative must carry the same licence.

## Les Misérables {#les-miserables}

```{=html}
<div class="ew-embed" data-network="les_miserables.gml"
     data-params="layout=force&colorAttr=modularity_community&sizeAttr=degree&labelAttr=label&edgeOpacity=0.7&edgeScale=2.4"
     data-caption="Les Misérables — 58 nodes, 168 edges, undirected"></div>
```

| | |
|---|---|
| **A node** | Character in Les Misérables, colored by narrative group |
| **An edge** | Two characters appear together in a scene, width ∝ number of shared scenes |

Knuth, D. E. (1993). The Stanford GraphBase: A Platform for Combinatorial Computing. Addison-Wesley.

*Donald E. Knuth · compiled by Max Jerdee · [source](https://www-cs-faculty.stanford.edu/~knuth/sgb.html) · [data and build script](https://github.com/maxjerdee/networks/tree/main/networks/les_miserables)*

**Licence.** No licence stated. From Knuth's Stanford GraphBase, distributed for public use and redistributed very widely (d3, networkx, igraph). Cite the book.

## Florentine Families {#florentine}

```{=html}
<div class="ew-embed" data-network="florentine.gml"
     data-params="layout=force&colorAttr=faction&labelAttr=label&edgeOpacity=0.233"
     data-caption="Florentine Families — 15 nodes, 20 edges, undirected"></div>
```

| | |
|---|---|
| **A node** | Florentine family, colored by faction |
| **An edge** | A marriage tie between the two families |

Padgett, J. F., & Ansell, C. K. (1993). Robust Action and the Rise of the Medici, 1400-1434. American Journal of Sociology, 98(6), 1259-1319.

*John F. Padgett and Christopher K. Ansell · [source](https://doi.org/10.1086/230190) · [data and build script](https://github.com/maxjerdee/networks/tree/main/networks/florentine)*

**Licence.** No licence stated by the source. Published as part of the cited paper, before data licensing was normal, and redistributed widely in the network-science literature since; there is no licence to point to. Cite the paper.

## Chicken Pecking Order {#chickens}

```{=html}
<div class="ew-embed" data-network="chickens.gml"
     data-params="layout=coord&coordYAttr=value&labelAttr=label&edgeOpacity=0.7"
     data-caption="Chicken Pecking Order — 11 nodes, 38 edges, directed"></div>
```

| | |
|---|---|
| **A node** | Hen, positioned by dominance rank |
| **An edge** | A → B: A pecks B (A dominates B) |

Masure, R. H., & Allee, W. C. (1934). The social order in flocks of the common chicken and the pigeon. The Auk, 51(3), 306-327.

*Ralph H. Masure and W. C. Allee · [source](https://doi.org/10.2307/4077659) · [data and build script](https://github.com/maxjerdee/networks/tree/main/networks/chickens)*

**Licence.** No licence stated by the source. Published as part of the cited paper, before data licensing was normal, and redistributed widely in the network-science literature since; there is no licence to point to. Cite the paper.

## English Football {#english-football}

```{=html}
<div class="ew-embed" data-network="english-football.gml"
     data-params="layout=coord&colorAttr=league&sizeAttr=degree&coordXAttr=league&coordYAttr=ds_score&edgeOpacity=0.35&edgeScale=0.5"
     data-caption="English Football — 426 nodes, 9572 edges, directed"></div>
```

| | |
|---|---|
| **A node** | Football club, colored by league tier |
| **An edge** | A → B: A beats B (or draws, if marked as a tie), 2024–25 season |

2024-25 English league football (levels 1-8) plus that season's FA Cup, compiled by Max Jerdee from Football Web Pages match grids downloaded 2026-02-19; one edge per game, winner to loser, draws as edges typed "neutral"; teams without a named league removed.

*Football Web Pages (footballwebpages.co.uk) · compiled by Max Jerdee · [source](https://www.footballwebpages.co.uk/) · [data and build script](https://github.com/maxjerdee/networks/tree/main/networks/english-football)*

**Licence.** Match results from Football Web Pages, whose terms state: "All of the information on this site is provided for free. Anybody may use it", provided the use is lawful and does not infringe others' rights (terms last reviewed June 2019; checked unchanged 2026-09-27, https://www.footballwebpages.co.uk/terms-and-conditions). They place no limit on redistribution and ask for no attribution; Football Web Pages is credited as the source regardless.
